=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Overall view:** This is not a "fair and balanced package". Read together, the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter do two things that cut against Wattlebridge: (1) they collapse every protection you would normally have (fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, fraud) into a single 20% / 18-month regime, and (2) they shift roughly **AUD 4.2m+ of known, quantified value leakage** onto the Company post-Completion while leaving the AUD 24m headline price untouched. The Disclosure Letter is also carefully drafted to disclose *facts* while admitting nothing — which is fine as a drafting device, but it means several items that look "addressed" in the Update are in fact completely unresolved on the Seller's own evidence.

I take the issues in order of materiality.

---

## A. Price / value-leakage issues (fix in the funds flow or the price)

### 1. Riverlark facility – AUD ~3.2m (Clauses 2 / 7)
**Seller position:** release "to be provided following Completion".
**Problem:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. If the AUD 3.2m facility is still outstanding at Completion and the price isn't adjusted, you pay AUD 24m for a company that still owes AUD 3.2m — you are effectively paying AUD 27.2m. The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility has **not** been repaid and **no** discharge is in the data room. Clause 8.1 of the facility also has a change-of-control trigger, so Completion itself probably puts the Company into default the moment the shares transfer.
**Push back:**
- Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price, via a payout letter from Riverlark delivered pre-Completion and itemised in the funds flow (Buyer pays Riverlark directly).
- Delivery at Completion of the executed release and discharge of all security (and PPSR/ASIC deregistration undertakings), plus Riverlark's consent/waiver of the 8.1 change-of-control default.
- Make delivery of these a Completion deliverable, not a post-Completion undertaking. Confirm whether Riverlark's security extends to the shares themselves — if so, it is also a title issue.

### 2. DD-005 closing bonuses – AUD 420k plus on-costs
**Seller position:** "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in the funds flow.
**Problem:** The Seller is not the employer — Paperbark is. Unless the funds flow carries them, these bonuses are paid by the Company you now own, out of cash you've paid for. On-costs are also undisclosed: superannuation (12%) and NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) on AUD 420k add roughly AUD 70–75k, so realistic exposure is ~AUD 490k–500k. The "continued-employment" condition also suggests some portion may be payable *after* Completion, i.e. a trailing liability.
**Push back:**
- Define the bonuses and all associated super, payroll tax and on-costs as **Transaction Expenses / Debt** deducted from the price, or have the Seller fund them through the funds flow at Completion.
- Require the bonus letters (DD-005) to be fully disclosed, with a schedule of amounts, payment dates and conditions, and a Seller indemnity for any shortfall.

### 3. Ironquay IP – SOW3 Project Materials (Clause 11.1)
**Seller position:** indemnity limited to "the specific Statement of Work 3 payment" and "considered adequate".
**Problem:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials does **not** pass until every SOW3 fee is paid. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. So on the current record, Paperbark does not own part of its own developed IP. An indemnity capped at the AUD 180k payment covers the cheque, not the consequence (inability to use/licence the IP, Ironquay asserting ownership, re-development cost, customer claims). The Disclosure Letter's point that DD-010 is "not independent bank verification of non-payment" is the Seller hedging — treat it as unpaid until proven otherwise.
**Push back:**
- CP or Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** an executed confirmatory assignment (and moral rights consents) from Ironquay.
- Failing that, deduct AUD 180k from the price and expand the specific indemnity to cover all loss arising from any defect in title to the Project Materials — outside the general cap and basket, 6-year survival.
- IP title warranty should be a fundamental warranty (see B.1).

### 4. Sandbar renewals – 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k
**Seller position:** "ordinary-course operating costs".
**Problem:** The Disclosure Letter itself says the material does not establish whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course — so the Update's characterisation is unsupported. Three identical AUD 110k contracts with the same supplier spread across DD-008 and DD-011 look like a single AUD 330k commitment split (possibly to sit under approval or materiality thresholds). If any part relates to the pre-Completion period or was committed outside the ordinary course, it belongs to the Seller.
**Push back:**
- Full copies of all three renewal contracts and the underlying services, with an explanation of why they were split.
- Any amount accrued/committed pre-Completion to be a Debt/working-capital item in the completion accounts (or, if locked box, Leakage).
- Ensure the SPA aggregates "a series of related claims" for de minimis purposes so the Seller can't argue each renewal is a separate matter.

**Cumulative:** Items 1–4 alone are **~AUD 4.2m** (3.2m + ~0.49m + 0.18m + 0.33m) of value that the Seller is currently leaving in the Company against a AUD 24m price. That is ~17.5% of the price and must be dealt with in the mechanics, not left to warranty claims that are then capped at 20% and subject to a basket.

---

## B. Liability regime (Clauses 9.3 / 12 / 13 / 20.5)

### 1. Fundamental and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits — **reject**
This is the single most off-market proposal in the package. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap the Seller's liability for not owning what it is selling at 20% of the price and 18 months. If title fails, you lose 100% of the price, not 20%.
**Position:** Capacity, authority, title to shares, no encumbrances, and (given Ironquay) ownership of core IP to be fundamental warranties: cap = 100% of price, survival of at least 6 years (7 for tax) or the statutory limitation period, and outside the de minimis/basket.

### 2. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" / limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" — **reject as drafted**
These two sentences, combined, are a drag-net: the 20% cap, AUD 250k basket, 18-month limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance language would apply to the Riverlark, bonus, Ironquay, data-incident and tax exposures above — exactly the items the limitations should *not* touch. The default rule inverts the market norm (limitations apply only where expressly stated).
**Position:** Express carve-outs from all caps, thresholds, time limits and the exclusive-remedy clause for: fraud/wilful concealment; fundamental warranties; the tax indemnity and tax warranties; each specific indemnity; Leakage / completion-accounts adjustments; breach of pre-Completion covenants and restraints; and liability that cannot be excluded by law (ACL misleading or deceptive conduct — a blanket non-reliance clause for "all Claims of any nature" is of doubtful effect against statutory claims anyway, so don't let the Seller pretend it is).

### 3. Quantum and time limits — negotiate, but in the market range
- **Cap 20% (AUD 4.8m):** Low end of the Australian mid-market range; given the known issues, push for 30–50%, or accept 20% only if the specific indemnities and fundamental warranties sit entirely outside it and the leakage items are fixed in the price.
- **Basket AUD 250k (~1%) excess-only:** Push for a tipping basket (recover from the first dollar once exceeded) or a lower deductible (~0.5%). De minimis AUD 25k is acceptable with a related-claims aggregation clause.
- **18 months:** Push for 24 months for general warranties (covers one full audit cycle post-Completion); tax 7 years; fundamental 6+ years.
- Add a reasonable period (e.g. 6–9 months) after notification to commence proceedings so the limitation isn't a trap.

### 4. Clause 8.3 Buyer knowledge — **reject the constructive-knowledge limb**
"Discoverable from the data room or public records" is a constructive-knowledge exclusion. Combined with general disclosure of the whole data room (Sched 7 / DL 1.1–1.2), it would mean *every* document, however buried or mis-indexed, qualifies *every* warranty, and anything you *could* have found on an ASIC or PPSR search is excluded regardless of whether it was found. That makes the warranties largely illusory.
**Position:**
- Knowledge limited to the *actual* knowledge of a named, short list of deal-team individuals, and only of matters not already covered by a specific indemnity.
- Disclosure only through the Disclosure Letter, against a **fair disclosure** standard (disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter). General disclosure of "the data room" and "publicly searchable records" either deleted or confined to specific listed documents fairly disclosed. If Seller insists on data-room disclosure, require a fixed, agreed index and a USB/hash of the room as at the cut-off.
- The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 Sept 2026 — six weeks ago. Any Completion bring-down must not permit new disclosures to qualify the Completion warranties without a corresponding Buyer termination right / price adjustment.

### 5. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" — **not settled**
Tax warranties and a standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, covering income tax, GST, payroll tax, super guarantee — note the bonus on-costs above) should survive 7 years at 100% cap. IP warranties should at minimum sit above the general cap given Ironquay demonstrates a live IP title defect.

---

## C. Conditions and deal-certainty issues

### 1. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3) — ~30% of revenue
**Seller position:** "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
**Problem:** The Disclosure Letter says no final consent exists and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. "Treat as satisfied on delivery of written consent" means a conditional or qualified consent (e.g. consent subject to a price concession, shorter term, or termination right) would satisfy the CP. For a customer worth AUD 3.6m p.a., that is unacceptable.
**Position:**
- CP: unconditional written consent from Bluefen to the change of control in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, with written evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived, and no amendment to pricing, term or termination rights.
- Seller obligation upgraded to "all reasonable endeavours" / "best endeavours" with Buyer participation in the approach to Bluefen.
- Fallback if not obtained: Buyer walk right, or a price adjustment / deferred consideration tied to Bluefen revenue retention over 12–18 months.
- Add a MAC condition and a specific warranty that no customer representing >5% of revenue has indicated an intention to terminate or renegotiate.

### 2. DD-006 data incident
**Seller position:** "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
**Problem:** ~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external recipient. Whether or not it is ultimately a notifiable "eligible data breach", the Company is obliged under the Privacy Act to assess within 30 days of becoming aware — and the incident predates 22 Sept, so that window has very likely already closed. Six weeks on, the Seller offers no update. Exposure includes OAIC notification obligations, civil penalties (substantially increased since 2022), customer-contract breach claims (check Bluefen/Mossvale confidentiality and data clauses), and remediation cost. The Seller's "no loss amount stated" is simply absence of analysis, not evidence of no loss.
**Position:**
- Immediate updated disclosure: assessment outcome, whether access occurred, whether OAIC/individuals were notified, legal advice relied on.
- Pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and make any required notifications before Completion, with Buyer consultation.
- Specific indemnity (uncapped or with its own cap, 6-year survival) for all loss, penalties, notification costs, third-party claims and remediation arising from DD-006, carved out of the general regime and not qualified by disclosure.
- Privacy and data-security warranties at Completion.

### 3. Title (DD-012 share register)
The Disclosure Letter expressly says the register is merely "the source relied on" and that the Buyer hasn't completed its own verification. Don't take the hint lightly: run a fresh ASIC search and PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, confirm the Seller's constitution/shareholder agreement has no pre-emptive rights or consent requirements, and confirm Riverlark's security does not extend to the shares. Title warranty = fundamental (see B.1).

### 4. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Lower risk, but tidy up: Seller to give the landlord notification pre-Completion with evidence delivered at Completion; confirm the Mossvale assignment clause does not define "assignment" to include change of control and obtain a warranty that no customer or supplier contract contains an unsatisfied change-of-control trigger (beyond those scheduled).

---

## D. Disclosure Letter drafting points
- **[1.4] non-admission:** acceptable as a general reservation, but the SPA must confirm that disclosure does not qualify the specific indemnities, the price adjustments, or the fundamental warranties.
- **[11] reservation:** the Seller is explicitly putting the evaluative burden on you — which is fine, but it undercuts the Update's "addressed / adequate / not material" characterisations. Where Update and Disclosure Letter conflict, cite the Disclosure Letter back to them.
- Require a bring-down Disclosure Letter at Completion with a Buyer right to terminate or adjust if new material matters emerge.

---

## E. Summary of recommendations (in priority order)

| # | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/title warranties under general cap and 18 months | Reject. 100% cap, 6–7 yr survival, outside basket. |
| 2 | Limitations apply to "all Claims" by default | Reject. Express carve-outs for fraud, fundamental, tax, specific indemnities, leakage, covenants, non-excludable statutory liability. |
| 3 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m released "post-Completion" | Repay at Completion from price via funds flow; payout letter, release, discharge of security and CoC waiver as Completion deliverables. |
| 4 | AUD 420k bonuses outside funds flow | Treat as Transaction Expense/Debt incl. super & payroll tax (~AUD 490k+); Seller funds; indemnity for any shortfall. |
| 5 | Bluefen consent "deemed satisfied on delivery" | CP for unconditional consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met, Buyer-satisfactory form; walk right or deferred consideration fallback; MAC. |
| 6 | Ironquay IP indemnity limited to AUD 180k payment | CP for payment + confirmatory assignment; otherwise deduct and give full uncapped IP-title indemnity. |
| 7 | Clause 8.3 constructive knowledge + general data-room disclosure | Actual knowledge of named individuals only; fair-disclosure standard; disclosure via Disclosure Letter only. |
| 8 | DD-006 data incident "not material" | Updated disclosure now; pre-Completion assessment/notification covenant; specific uncapped indemnity; privacy warranties. |
| 9 | Sandbar AUD 330k renewals | Produce contracts; pre-Completion commitments as Debt/Leakage; related-claims aggregation. |
| 10 | Cap 20% / basket excess-only / 18 months | Push 30–50%, tipping basket, 24 months general, 7 years tax. |
| 11 | Tax/IP "settled" | Separate tax indemnity 7 yrs at 100%; IP warranties above general cap. |
| 12 | Title evidence | Independent ASIC/PPSR verification; confirm no pre-emption/encumbrances on shares. |
| 13 | Lease / Mossvale | Evidence of landlord notification at Completion; CoC warranty across material contracts. |
| 14 | Disclosure Letter dated 22 Sept | Bring-down at Completion with Buyer termination/adjustment right; disclosure not to qualify indemnities or fundamentals. |

**Suggested framing for the response to Seller counsel:** the AUD 24m price was agreed on a debt-free/cash-free basis with clean title and the Bluefen relationship intact. The package as drafted leaves ~AUD 4.2m of known liabilities in the Company, leaves the largest customer and core IP unsecured, and then caps your recourse for all of it at AUD 4.8m for 18 months. Either the mechanics fix the known items at Completion, or the price does.

One caveat: I have worked from the Seller's summary of the clauses, not the SPA text itself. Several points (particularly the scope of "Claims", the exclusive-remedy clause, and whether the price mechanism is locked-box or completion accounts) should be checked against the actual draft before the mark-up goes back. Happy to prepare the clause-by-clause rider if you can share the SPA.

**Position:**
- Knowledge limited to the *actual* knowledge of a named, short list of deal-team individuals, and only of matters not already covered by a specific indemnity.
- Disclosure only through the Disclosure Letter, against a **fair disclosure** standard (disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter). General disclosure of "the data room" and "publicly searchable records" either deleted or confined to specific listed documents fairly disclosed. If Seller insists on data-room disclosure, require a fixed, agreed index and a USB/hash of the room as at the cut-off.
- The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 Sept 2026 — six weeks ago. Any Completion bring-down must not permit new disclosures to qualify the Completion warranties without a corresponding Buyer termination right / price adjustment.

### 5. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" — **not settled**
Tax warranties and a standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, covering income tax, GST, payroll tax, super guarantee — note the bonus on-costs above) should survive 7 years at 100% cap. IP warranties should at minimum sit above the general cap given Ironquay demonstrates a live IP title defect.

## C. Conditions and deal-certainty issues

### 1. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3) — ~30% of revenue
**Seller position:** "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
**Problem:** The Disclosure Letter says no final consent exists and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. "Treat as satisfied on delivery of written consent" means a conditional or qualified consent (e.g. consent subject to a price concession, shorter term, or termination right) would satisfy the CP. For a customer worth AUD 3.6m p.a., that is unacceptable.
**Position:**
- CP: unconditional written consent from Bluefen to the change of control in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, with written evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived, and no amendment to pricing, term or termination rights.
- Seller obligation upgraded to "all reasonable endeavours" / "best endeavours" with Buyer participation in the approach to Bluefen.
- Fallback if not obtained: Buyer walk right, or a price adjustment / deferred consideration tied to Bluefen revenue retention over 12–18 months.
- Add a MAC condition and a specific warranty that no customer representing >5% of revenue has indicated an intention to terminate or renegotiate.

### 2. DD-006 data incident
**Seller position:** "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
**Problem:** ~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external recipient. Whether or not it is ultimately a notifiable "eligible data breach", the Company is obliged under the Privacy Act to assess within 30 days of becoming aware — and the incident predates 22 Sept, so that window has very likely already closed. Six weeks on, the Seller offers no update. Exposure includes OAIC notification obligations, civil penalties (substantially increased since 2022), customer-contract breach claims (check Bluefen/Mossvale confidentiality and data clauses), and remediation cost. The Seller's "no loss amount stated" is simply absence of analysis, not evidence of no loss.
**Position:**
- Immediate updated disclosure: assessment outcome, whether access occurred, whether OAIC/individuals were notified, legal advice relied on.
- Pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and make any required notifications before Completion, with Buyer consultation.
- Specific indemnity (uncapped or with its own cap, 6-year survival) for all loss, penalties, notification costs, third-party claims and remediation arising from DD-006, carved out of the general regime and not qualified by disclosure.
- Privacy and data-security warranties at Completion.

### 3. Title (DD-012 share register)
The Disclosure Letter expressly says the register is merely "the source relied on" and that the Buyer hasn't completed its own verification. Don't take the hint lightly: run a fresh ASIC search and PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, confirm the Seller's constitution/shareholder agreement has no pre-emptive rights or consent requirements, and confirm Riverlark's security does not extend to the shares. Title warranty = fundamental (see B.1).

### 4. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Lower risk, but tidy up: Seller to give the landlord notification pre-Completion with evidence delivered at Completion; confirm the Mossvale assignment clause does not define "assignment" to include change of control and obtain a warranty that no customer or supplier contract contains an unsatisfied change-of-control trigger (beyond those scheduled).

## D. Disclosure Letter drafting points
- **[1.4] non-admission:** acceptable as a general reservation, but the SPA must confirm that disclosure does not qualify the specific indemnities, the price adjustments, or the fundamental warranties.
- **[11] reservation:** the Seller is explicitly putting the evaluative burden on you — which is fine, but it undercuts the Update's "addressed / adequate / not material" characterisations. Where Update and Disclosure Letter conflict, cite the Disclosure Letter back to them.
- Require a bring-down Disclosure Letter at Completion with a Buyer right to terminate or adjust if new material matters emerge.
